entries.title: AI as a learning partner
entries.summary: A UCL Changemakers study cites my work with Nina Dethlefs when exploring how conversational AI can support student confidence, seminar preparation and participation.
entries.source_title: Repositioning GenAI as a Dialogic Learning Partner
entries.evidence: The discussion connects the idea of a chatbot as a friend, guide or philosopher to students rehearsing seminar contributions. The paper explicitly cites Chatterjee and Dethlefs (2023).
entries.publication_title: This new conversational AI model can be your friend, philosopher, and guide, and even your worst enemy

entries.title: Quoted in guidance for PhD researchers
entries.summary: PhD on Track quotes our conversational AI paper in its guidance on research practice, bringing the work into a resource designed for doctoral researchers.
entries.evidence: The Opportunities section quotes the title of our Patterns paper under LLMs as conversation partners. UiT describes PhD on Track as a collaboration between five Norwegian university libraries.
entries.publication_title: This new conversational AI model can be your friend, philosopher, and guide, and even your worst enemy

entries.title: How universities respond to generative AI
entries.summary: A study of three Swedish universities cites our work in its analysis of how people understand and relate to conversational AI, from initial suspicion to acceptance as a colleague or collaborator.
entries.source_title: From villain to VIP: institutional responses to generative AI in higher education
entries.evidence: Published in the Journal of Professions and Organization, October 2026. The theoretical discussion and analysis reference Chatterjee and Dethlefs (2023) on human-like qualities and roles attributed to AI.
entries.publication_title: This new conversational AI model can be your friend, philosopher, and guide, and even your worst enemy

entries.organization: Singapore University of Technology and Design
entries.title: AI-assisted research on ageing and technology
entries.summary: Researchers at SUTD and collaborating institutions cite our work in developing an AI prompting procedure for analysing older adults’ perceptions of ageing and technology.
entries.source_title: Codesign and AI: AI-assisted clustering of perception patterns of seniors on ageing and technology in Singapore
entries.evidence: Section 3.2 references Chatterjee and Dethlefs (2023) while describing the structured procedure and SCOPE framework for AI prompting. Published by Cambridge University Press in Proceedings of the Design Society.
entries.publication_title: This new conversational AI model can be your friend, philosopher, and guide, and even your worst enemy

entries.title: Explainable AI assessed in a systematic review
entries.summary: A review of 48 studies includes our wind-turbine anomaly prediction research. Its comparative analysis highlights fault explanations that align with human analysis.
entries.source_title: Renewable energy management using explainable artificial intelligence
entries.evidence: Tables 3 and 11 and the wind-energy discussion assess our 2020 Wind Energy paper, including feature importance for fault diagnosis. This is an independent review of the method, not a new deployment claim.
entries.publication_title: Deep learning with knowledge transfer for explainable anomaly prediction in wind turbines

entries.title: Among 100 highly cited LLM publications studied
entries.summary: An independent bibliometric study includes our early ChatGPT paper among the publications it analyses, citing its emphasis on human oversight for reliable AI outputs.
entries.source_title: Identification and Categorization of the Top 100 Articles and the Future of Large Language Models: Thematic Analysis Using Bibliometric Analysis
entries.evidence: Our paper is reference 80, within the reviewed technology and information sciences group. The discussion cites it on human oversight. The 100-publication selection belongs to this study and its search criteria, rather than a current universal ranking.
entries.publication_title: This new conversational AI model can be your friend, philosopher, and guide, and even your worst enemy

entries.title: ReActV in the discussion on human agency
entries.summary: The society’s adaptive and interactive systems group discusses our co-authored ReActV delivery-planning research as an example of AI supporting workers while retaining human intervention and control.
entries.source_title: ABIS@WebSci 2026: The Effects of the Adaptive Web on Society
entries.evidence: The official workshop reflection names all four co-authors and describes stepwise confirmation and escalation in the proposed system. It discusses human agency in algorithmically managed work environments.
entries.publication_title: Structuring the Last Mile with ReActV: Tool-Augmented Delivery Planning with Verification
